senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; preced.) [pleasure, will (Jonah III, 7),]
sense, wisdom, sound reasoning; reason, cause, ground.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 18a:7">Ab. Zar. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>דברים של ט׳</he> sensible argument.
<cite ref="Chullin 6a:5">Ḥull. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>להחזיר לו ט׳</he> to give him a clear answer.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 83b:9">Sabb. 83ᵇ</cite> <he>ולא נתגלה טַעֲמָהּ</he> the reason of it has not been made known.
<cite ref="Chullin 101b:8">Ḥull. 101ᵇ</cite> <he>מאיזה ט׳ וכ׳</he> for what reason it has been forbidden to them; a. fr.—Pl. <he>טְעָמִים</he>, <he>טְעָמִין</he>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 34a:12">Snh. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>מקרא אחד יוצא לכמה ט׳ ואין טעם אחד וכ׳</he> one biblical expression may be used for many arguments, but one and the same argument must not be deduced from different biblical expressions.
Erub. 13ᵇ טַעֲמֵי טומאה arguments in favor of uncleanness; a. fr.—פִּסְקי טְעָמִים the incisions, in the Bible verse, according to sense; punctuation signs, accents.
Meg. 3ᵃ (ref. to ויבינו במקרא, Neh. VIII, 8) אלו פ׳ ט׳ that means the punctuation signs; Y. ib. IV, 74ᵈ bot.; Gen. R. s. 36 (ref. to ושום שכל, Neh. l. c.) אלו הט׳ (sub. פסקי).—Esp. taste.
<cite ref="Chullin 98b:12">Ḥull. 98ᵇ</cite> <he>ט׳ כעיקר</he> the taste of a forbidden thing is as forbidden as the substance itself.
<cite ref="Pesachim 44b:17">Pes. 44ᵇ</cite> top <he>ליתן ט׳ כעיקר</he> to intimate that the taste (of grapes soaked in water) is equally forbidden as the substance (of grapes).
<cite ref="Chullin 108a:3">Ḥull. 108ᵃ</cite> <he>טַעֲמוֹ ולא ממשו וכ׳</he> the taste of a thing without the substance (after removing the forbidden substance) is in all cases biblically forbidden.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 7:4">Ib. VII, 4</cite> <he>אם יש בה בנותן ט׳</he> if there is enough of it to give a taste to the entire mixture.

<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 7:4">Ib.</cite> <he>בזמן שמכירו בנותן ט׳</he> as long as it can be recognized (and removed), it depends on its giving a taste (whether or not the mixture is forbidden). Ib. 111ᵇ <he>נותן ט׳ בר נותן ט׳</he> an object forbidden for its having absorbed the taste of a forbidden thing, and which (through mixture) has again given taste to another thing, a taste-giver in the second degree.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 39b:16">Ab. Zar. 39ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>נותן טעם לפגם</he> (abbr. <he>נ״ט</he>) imparting a deteriorating taste, <he>נ״ט לשבח</he> giving an improving taste; a. v. fr.—
